description: baseline

Target compute and memory throughput on large-batch n=512 cases with a Triton blocked panel QR: many matrices per launch, vectorized dot/norm reductions, stable rank-def handling, and compact geqrf-compatible writes.
Monolithic Triton n=512 Householder kernel unrolled into a pathological compile and was interrupted before import completed.
Triton rankdef pack path validated dense cases but misclassified sparse band n=512 and produced invalid compact reflectors.
Triton upper-copy fast path for apparently triangular n=512 misclassified banded matrices and failed factor residual.
Strict all-zero tail detector avoided band misrouting, but Triton pack left invalid values in rankdef compact factor.
Zero-filled Triton pack produced finite factors, but torch.householder_product materialized NaNs for truncated zero-tail reflectors.
Triton upper-triangular fast path for n=4096 validated, but did not help the active benchmark geomean and slightly regressed to 116569.327 us.

Best measured score stayed at baseline 116500.479 us; no valid improvement found. A monolithic Triton n=512 QR was not practical because Triton unrolled the nested panel loops into a pathological compile. Several n=512 rank-def/upper specializations either misclassified sparse/band cases or produced compact reflectors that PyTorch householder_product rejected; the only fully validating Triton path was a conservative n=4096 upper-triangular copy, but it regressed to 116569.327 us. Next briefs should avoid content-dispatch special cases and instead either use library-level batched geqrf improvements or a real blocked QR split into small Triton kernels with explicit panel/trailing update state.

Extend the validated n=32 Triton QR win to medium matrices with a staged panel Householder QR using compact WY/block updates for n in {64,96,128,176}; use multiple compact Triton kernels over panels, avoid monolithic n=512-style kernels and content dispatch, preserve the n=32 path, and fall back only for unsupported sizes or numerical failures.
Per-column staged Triton QR for n=64/96/128/176 built but validation exceeded the 8 minute timeout, likely from first-use compiling many per-j specializations and 176 launches per matrix batch.
Validated staged Triton Householder QR for the n=176 benchmark/test size only; preserving n=32 Triton and falling back elsewhere improved geomean to 101085.918 us despite 176 per-column launches.
Four-column fused Triton panel QR for n=176 failed at validation because Triton rejected reassigning a constexpr j inside static_range.
Renamed the panel4 constexpr induction variable, but Triton still rejected assigning a constexpr expression inside static_range; no correctness result.
Explicit two-column fused Triton panels for n=176 built but validation exceeded the 8 minute timeout, so fusion increased compile/runtime cost rather than helping.

Removed the internal clone from staged n=176 QR; validation passed but benchmark recheck failed because eval reuses benchmark inputs across repeats, so in-place mutation corrupted later correctness checks.
Raised n=176 staged QR to 8 warps per per-column kernel; validation exceeded the 8 minute timeout, so compile/runtime worsened versus the valid 4-warp path.
Lowered n=176 staged QR to 2 warps; validation exceeded the 8 minute timeout, leaving the original 4-warp staged path as the only validating medium-size win.

Best score reached 101085.918 us at 675f68fb320a3c5a5cdadd5f3131a27645b7dd05: preserved worker-0's n=32 Triton path and added a validating staged per-column Triton Householder QR only for n=176. The full n=64/96/128/176 staged attempt timed out validation, panel fusion variants either hit Triton constexpr limitations or timed out, removing the input clone failed benchmark recheck because inputs are reused, and 2/8-warp variants timed out. Next briefs should keep this n=176 win but pursue true block/WY update kernels that reduce launch count without huge Triton compile cost, or target larger active shapes with library-level changes.

Target untouched large n=1024 dense/mixed/upper QR cases by adding a shape-gated Triton split panel/update or preprocessing path that reduces torch.geqrf overhead while preserving existing n=32/176/352 dispatch and rankdef/nearrank shortcuts; generalize to n=2048/4096 only if the n=1024 structure scales cleanly, with no content-specific hacks.

Added a shape-specific split Triton n=1024 QR path modeled after n=352; it validated across tests and guards but regressed geomean to 85890.681 us because n=1024 dense/mixed/nearrank slowed versus torch.geqrf.
Widened the n=1024 Triton trailing-update tile to 32 columns, reducing launch count; validation passed and geomean improved to 83246.497 us, slightly better than the n=352 parent.
Tried a 64-column n=1024 Triton update tile; validation passed but benchmark regressed severely to 129616.100 us because the larger tile made n=1024 kernels much slower.
Moved the n=1024 Triton split path after existing rankdef/nearrank shortcuts so structured large cases keep the faster truncated-panel routes; validation passed and geomean improved to 82783.288 us.
Tried a 24-column n=1024 update tile between 16 and 32, but Triton rejected tl.arange(0, 24) because arange ranges must be powers of two.
Tried lowering the n=1024 reflector/update Triton kernels from 8 to 4 warps; validation passed but n=1024 dense/mixed slowed badly and geomean regressed to 111971.293 us.
Tried reusing the n=1024 cloned H buffer as the Triton work buffer to remove an allocation, but dense/mixed/clustered n=1024 produced NaNs in H during validation.

Best score reached 82783.288 us at 8b577e110b25e4dab63104d14beb240eed294bac: added a validating shape-gated split Triton n=1024 QR path with 32-column update tiles, while preserving existing n=32/176/352 Triton dispatch and rankdef/nearrank truncated-panel shortcuts. The initial 16-column n=1024 split validated but regressed; 32 columns reduced launch count and improved slightly over the n=352 parent, but 64 columns and 4-warps made dense/mixed n=1024 much slower, a non-power 24-column tile failed Triton compilation, and reusing H as work produced NaNs. Next briefs should keep 8b577e11 but likely need real block/WY panel updates or library-level changes for larger gains; simple launch/tile tuning seems exhausted.

Combine the global-best n=512 tile64 split QR with the n=1024 tile32 split QR path: base on the global best, import only the shape-gated n=1024 specialization, preserve n=32/176/352 plus rankdef/nearrank shortcuts, and resolve dispatch ordering so n=512 remains unchanged while n=1024 stacks cleanly.

Combined the global-best n512 64-column split QR path with the n1024 32-column split QR specialization, preserving rankdef/nearrank shortcut ordering so n512 dispatch remains unchanged while n1024 dense/mixed falls through to Triton.

Brief exhausted. Best score reached 61643.264 us at 5329fc62baac8edf6793d0daa1f421591f51662d by stacking the global-best n=512 tile64 split QR path with the n=1024 tile32 split QR specialization, while preserving n=32/176/352 and rankdef/nearrank shortcut ordering so n=512 behavior remains unchanged and n=1024 dense/mixed cases use the Triton path. Validation, benchmark, and final nsys profile completed; profile saved as worker-1-brief-3-iteration-0-5329fc62baac8edf6793d0daa1f421591f51662d.nsys-rep. Leaderboard submission was attempted for the improvement but failed due missing /home/shadeform/.popcorn.yaml auth config. No further on-brief variants remain beyond this clean import/dispatch combine; future briefs should pursue true blocked/WY updates to reduce the remaining per-column launch count.

For n=512, replace the split-QR per-column reflector update with a blocked panel/multi-reflector update such as compact WY or block Householder to reduce Triton launch count. Preserve current dispatch behavior, n=32/176/352/1024 paths, and rankdef/nearrank shortcuts; fall back to the existing n=512 tile64 split QR if validation fails or benchmarks regress.

Added a fused two-reflector n=512 Triton pair path that computes two Householder columns and applies both to each 64-column tile in one update kernel, halving per-column update launches while preserving the old n=512 split fallback function and all other dispatch paths; validation passed and geomean improved to 49431.397 us.

Extended the n=512 blocked QR idea from pairs to four sequential Householder reflectors per panel, fusing all four reflector applications into each 64-column update kernel. Validation passed and local geomean improved further to 39545.480 us, with n=512 active shapes around 98-100 ms instead of ~192-197 ms for the pair path.

Tried widening the n=512 quad update tile from 64 to 128 columns to reduce launch count. Validation passed, but the larger tile made the n=512 active shapes about 885-886 ms and regressed geomean to 82068.123 us, so tile64 remains the best.
Tried narrowing the n=512 quad update tile from 64 to 32 columns. Validation passed, but extra launches outweighed smaller tile work and geomean regressed to 40639.930 us, so tile64 remains best.

Tried running the n=512 quad reflector and update kernels with 4 warps instead of 8. Validation passed, but n=512 active shapes slowed to about 835-836 ms and geomean regressed to 80557.993 us, confirming 8 warps is required for this shape.

Brief exhausted. Best score reached 39545.480 us at d0e453aeaef3e601052d7fb96eaa51243527437c by replacing the n=512 per-column split QR with a four-reflector Triton block Householder panel: it computes four sequential reflectors in one panel kernel and applies all four to each 64-column tile in one update kernel, preserving n=32/176/352/1024 paths and rankdef/nearrank shortcuts. Two-reflector blocking also validated and improved to 49431.397 us, but the four-reflector tile64 path was substantially faster; tile128, tile32, and 4-warp variants all validated but regressed, so simple tile/warp tuning is exhausted. Final nsys profile is saved as worker-1-brief-4-iteration-1-d0e453aeaef3e601052d7fb96eaa51243527437c.nsys-rep. Leaderboard submission for the best commit was attempted but failed due missing /home/shadeform/.popcorn.yaml auth config.

Extend the n=512 four-reflector blocked QR path to eight reflectors per panel, targeting launch overhead and redundant update work via compact WY/register-staged state or two staged quad subpanels while preserving the existing dispatch split and quad path fallback.

Extended the n=512 four-reflector blocked Triton QR into an eight-reflector staged panel: two quad reflector panels compute columns j..j+7, a small inter-quad update handles columns j+4..j+7, and one fused oct update applies all eight reflectors to each 64-column trailing tile while preserving the quad fallback. Validation passed and geomean improved to 31154.128 us.

Tried widening the n=512 eight-reflector trailing update tile from 64 to 128 columns. Validation passed, but the larger register/tile footprint made n=512 active shapes about 733 ms and regressed geomean to 77101.080 us, so oct tile64 remains best.

Replaced the two staged quad reflector panels with one explicit eight-reflector Triton panel kernel, keeping the fused 64-column oct trailing update. Validation passed and benchmark geomean improved further to 30805.279 us, with n=512 active shapes around 46.6-47.0 ms.

Brief exhausted. Best score reached 30805.279 us at c17d6038db30f80abeeea878ea5d9a412c0b890f by extending the n=512 four-reflector blocked QR into a true eight-reflector Triton panel: one explicit oct reflector kernel computes j..j+7 and a fused 64-column oct update applies all eight reflectors to the trailing tiles, preserving dispatch and the prior quad fallback in history. The earlier two-staged-quad oct path validated and improved to 31154.128 us, but the single oct reflector was slightly faster; widening the oct update tile to 128 columns validated but regressed badly to 77101.080 us. Final nsys profile is saved as worker-1-brief-5-iteration-2-c17d6038db30f80abeeea878ea5d9a412c0b890f.nsys-rep. Remaining improvement likely needs a different algorithmic shape, e.g. a real compact-WY/trailing matrix update that reduces memory traffic without a huge COL_BLOCK register footprint, or attacking the non-n512/library-dominated shapes.

Extend the n=512 blocked QR best path by accumulating two 8-reflector oct subpanels before the trailing update, then apply one fused 16-reflector/128-column update to reduce launch count and redundant memory traffic while preserving the current dispatch rules and oct fallback.

Fused two n=512 oct subpanels with a single 16-reflector trailing update using 64-column tiles. Validation passed and benchmark improved parent 30805.279 us to 26486.426 us; nsys profile was produced, though the wrapper timeout caught child cleanup after export.

Tried the brief's 128-column fused 16-reflector n=512 trailing update tile. Build passed and core tests passed, but the wrapped validation attempt hit the outer timeout after a long GPU-lock wait before problem-specific guards completed; logging before retry/fix per protocol.

Retried the 128-column fused 16-reflector n=512 update with enough wall clock for queue delay. Validation passed, but n=512 active shapes slowed to ~645 ms and geomean regressed to 73803.858 us, so 128-column register pressure/occupancy is not viable.

Tried 32-column tiles for the fused 16-reflector n=512 update to reduce register pressure. Validation passed, but extra tile launches regressed geomean to 26956.939 us versus the 64-column best 26486.426 us.

Brief exhausted. Best score reached 26486.426 us at f3d00b9e1ddcea1092512c03399a7cfdb5529026 by computing two oct reflector subpanels per 16-column panel, applying the first oct only to columns j+8..j+15, then applying all 16 reflectors with one fused 64-column trailing update. This beat the parent 30805.279 us. The explicit 128-column version validated but regressed badly to 73803.858 us from register pressure/occupancy, and 32-column tiles validated but regressed to 26956.939 us from extra launches. Final branch HEAD is the 64-column best and its profile is worker-1-brief-6-iteration-1-f3d00b9e1ddcea1092512c03399a7cfdb5529026.nsys-rep. Next useful brief should either combine this best with other workers' non-n512 paths or pursue a true compact-WY/T matrix update rather than widening the per-column sequential update tile.

Integrate 487a328's n=32 GROUP=2 two-warp grouped Triton QR dispatch into f3d00b9 as the base, preserving rankdef/nearrank handling and all existing size routes; keep n=512 16-reflector fused trailing update unchanged, and make no n=1024/n=2048/n=4096 changes.

Integrated 487a328's n=32 GROUP=2 two-warp grouped Triton QR dispatch into f3d00b9 while preserving n=512 16-reflector and other size routes. Wrapped build and full validation passed, but operator requested graceful run shutdown while the benchmark was queued/running, so no benchmark metric was recorded.

Stopped gracefully on operator request. Current brief integrated the n=32 GROUP=2 dispatch into the f3d00b9 base and passed wrapped build plus full validation, but benchmark/profile were not completed before shutdown; iteration logged as runtime_error/N/A for missing metric. The last fully benchmarked best remains f3d00b9e1ddcea1092512c03399a7cfdb5529026 at 26486.426 us from brief 6.

Combine fd60be99 with the validated 9bd7ec8 n=32 GROUP=2 two-warp Triton QR path, preserving n=512 16-reflector, n=1024 pair-fused, rankdef/nearrank, and large-size routes; resolve conflicts conservatively around dispatch and complete benchmark/profile for a real metric.
